newsitem.title: UK: INSTANT VIEW - UK Jan retail sales, Jan minutes.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - UK Jan retail sales, Jan minutes.

text.p: January retail sales rose 0.6 percent month-on-month and were up 4.6 percent year-on-year. Following are analysts reactions to data.

"They are bang in line with expectations the underlying economy is picking up momentum. It's going to continue to fuel arguements from the Bank of England for a rate hike at some stage, but it's not going to soften Clarke's call for unchanged rates. "

"Stronger than expectations. There is fairly robust underlying growth in retail sales still. So the theory that things are beginning to slow down, which in our view has always been exaggerated, may not be right. On interest rates Clarke is resisting fairly strong calls from George for rate increases. George looks as if he has toned it down a little bit, but not hugely."

"They were above expectations, but the underlying trend is consistent with the modest pace of spending. They suggest the Bank of England will continue to push for higher rates. The Chancellor is likely to rebuff any calls for a tightening until after the election."

"Retail sales picked up in January as suggested by M0 and CBI and BRC surveys. It showed that Christmas sales were not actually weak but just carried over from December to January. The trend in consumption is slower than a few months ago, but still brisk enough to carry an inflation risk."

"The minutes show a very clear opposition between Clarke and George. Conflicts are likely to continue until the balance of power on monetary policy is changed by granting more independence to the BoE."
